title: PHARM · Serotonin syndrome (FAST AND TWITCHY) vs neuroleptic malignant syndrome (SLOW AND STIFF) (high stakes, night shift)

hook_backups: Nurses: sertraline plus tramadol. Why are her legs jerking?

save_card.title: SEROTONIN SYNDROME vs NMS
items: Serotonin syndrome (FAST AND TWITCHY): hours after a serotonin drug; jerking, shivering, sweating, diarrhea
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (SLOW AND STIFF): days after an antipsychotic; lead-pipe rigidity, slow responses
Both: high fever, fast heart rate, BP swings
Both: stop the drug, report now, cool

memory_line: Serotonin: fast and twitchy. NMS: slow and stiff.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 1:30 AM. She's 68, day 1 after a knee replacement.
• Takes sertraline (an SSRI, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) every day
• New order: tramadol for pain
• Now: sweating, shivering, legs jerking. 38.9 °C (102 °F), heart rate 122

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ Called it a post-op fever
2️⃣ Gave the next tramadol dose
3️⃣ Never reported the jerking legs or checked her meds
➡️ 40.4 °C (104.7 °F), rigid, a seizure. Rapid response.

🔥 Two drug reactions, both with a high fever

⚡ Serotonin syndrome (FAST AND TWITCHY)
• Hours after starting or raising a serotonin drug: SSRIs, tramadol, linezolid, triptans and more
• Jerking muscles (clonus), tremor, shivering, sweating, diarrhea, agitation
• Stop the serotonin drugs, report now. Cooling, benzodiazepines, cyproheptadine, as ordered

🧊 Neuroleptic malignant syndrome, NMS (SLOW AND STIFF)
• Days to weeks after an antipsychotic like haloperidol
• Lead-pipe rigidity (stiff all over), slow responses, confusion
• Stop the antipsychotic, report now. Cooling, fluids, treatment as ordered

✅ The right move
• New fever with jerking or rigidity? Check the med list first
• Hold the trigger drug and call

🧠 Serotonin: fast and twitchy. NMS: slow and stiff.
share_line: 📤 Send this to the nurse who'd call it a post-op fever.
sources: Tramadol hydrochloride prescribing information (DailyMed): serotonin syndrome warning
rn_checks: Serotonin syndrome: usually within hours (often within 24 h) of starting or raising a serotonergic drug; clonus, hyperreflexia, tremor, shivering, diaphoresis, diarrhea, agitation, hyperthermia
Sertraline plus tramadol is a labeled serotonin syndrome interaction (tramadol label)
NMS: days to weeks after an antipsychotic; lead-pipe rigidity, bradyreflexia, altered mental status, hyperthermia, high CK (creatine kinase)

Treatments named: SS = stop the drug, cooling, benzodiazepines, cyproheptadine as ordered; NMS = stop the antipsychotic, cooling, fluids, treatment as ordered (dantrolene not named here because it features in the 1 am malignant hyperthermia Reel)
Story numbers: 38.9 then 40.4 °C, heart rate 122, BP 168/96, rigidity and seizure. Realistic?
